intended_object: The determinant det(G) of the Gram matrix of a nondegenerate integral lattice (it does not depend on the basis), viewed as an element of ℚˣ. The library uses it to compare with the discriminant (square class in ℚˣ/(ℚˣ)²) of the rational quadratic space. This comes from the docstring and from its use in RationalInvariants.lean.
explanation:
`L.determinant` is the determinant of the integral Gram matrix in a chosen ℤ-basis of the lattice. The library proves it is the same in every basis (`gramDet_eq_gramDet`), so it is the standard signed determinant of an integral lattice, as in Ebeling, *Lattices and Codes*. `determinantUnit` casts this integer to ℚ and packages it as a unit with `Units.mk0`. The proof that it is nonzero uses `determinant_ne_zero_iff`: the determinant is nonzero exactly when the ambient rational form is nondegenerate, and nondegeneracy is the instance hypothesis `IsNondegenerate`. So the underlying value is exactly the Gram determinant, as the lemma `coe_determinantUnit` states.

Requiring nondegeneracy is not an extra restriction: it is exactly the condition under which the determinant is a unit of ℚ. Working over ℚ fits the library's setting of integral lattices inside rational vector spaces. ℚˣ is the natural target here because the value is used to form a square class in ℚˣ/(ℚˣ)². Mathlib has no notion of an integral lattice's determinant to compare against, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
